overview: Lean redesign of the gastroenterology central intake from January to June 2027: a value stream map with nurses, clerks and two family doctors, then A3 cycles that first remove intake rework (a returned-referral queue and a fixed daily triage time) and then release the structured template with a documented exception when a rapid test is unavailable.
population: All adult gastroenterology referrals received by the central intake from 160 family practices; a twelve-week baseline from October to December 2026.
exposure: Returned-referral queue with a tracked status visible to practices; fixed daily triage time; structured template with required fields for the six most common referral reasons, released on the digital health office's monthly schedule.
procedures: Weeks 1 to 2: value stream mapping and A3 problem statement. From week 3: the returned-referral queue and fixed triage time. From the April 2027 release: the template. The intake extracts weekly counts from the referral system; a random sample of 20 referrals a week is reviewed for bypass (an attached letter instead of the required fields). Practice workload is sampled by asking five practices a month to time template completion.

outcomes.name: Returned referrals
outcomes.measure: Weekly proportion of referrals returned for missing information
outcomes.why: The main failure the redesign targets and the one the evidence says templates can change.

outcomes.name: Time to triage decision
outcomes.measure: Weekly median working days from receipt to triage decision
outcomes.why: The access outcome on which the evidence conflicts (claim c3).

outcomes.name: Template bypass
outcomes.measure: Proportion of sampled referrals with an attached letter instead of completed fields
outcomes.why: High bypass would mean the template shifted work without improving information.

outcomes.name: Practice completion time
outcomes.measure: Minutes to complete a template, timed by five practices a month
outcomes.why: Practice workload is the main cost of templates (claim c4).

outcomes.name: Urgent referrals with a test result
outcomes.measure: Proportion of urgent lower gastrointestinal referrals with a faecal immunochemical test result
outcomes.why: Shows whether the required field works for the referrals where it matters most.

feasibility: Weekly counts come from the referral system; bypass review takes about one hour a week of clerk time; the lean coach supports the A3 cycles for three months.
biasMitigation: Countermeasures introduced in sequence with dates on the charts
Random weekly sample for bypass review
Returned referrals reported by practice group, including practices without rapid kits

biasFlags.label: Referral volume changes
biasFlags.note: Seasonal volume may move lead time; plot volume alongside.

biasFlags.label: Overlapping countermeasures
biasFlags.note: Queue and template effects are separated only by timing.

biasFlags.label: Unmeasured practice burden
biasFlags.note: Timing by five practices a month is a small sample.

flags: Two balancing measures and one process measure
No statistical adjustment; run and control charts only
parsimony.simplestPath: One intake, one primary measure on a p-chart, countermeasures in sequence.

theoreticalFramework: Lean thinking: value stream mapping, A3 problem solving and standard work; no additional framework.
summary: Six-month lean redesign with returned referrals as the primary measure and bypass and practice time as balancing measures.
